samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=embodied_robotics; abstract_task=industrial_logic_and_compliance. Task objective: test industrial_logic_and_compliance capability inside the embodied_robotics industrial domain. Scene family: erob_agv_rollup_door_interlock. Core scenario: AGV approaches a closed roll-up door; interlock holds the vehicle until the door opens and the path is clear. Reference subject: warehouse agv roll up door safety interlock. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Warehouse AGV, forklift, roll-up door, dock gate, or automated barrier with clear travel path. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: AGV approaches a closed roll-up door; interlock holds the vehicle until the door opens and the path is clear. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: warehouse agv roll up door safety interlock; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (warehouse agv roll up door safety interlock); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Warehouse AGV, forklift, roll-up door, dock gate, or automated barrier with clear travel path.. samples.prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=embodied_robotics; abstract_task=industrial_logic_and_compliance. Task objective: test industrial_logic_and_compliance capability inside the embodied_robotics industrial domain. Scene family: erob_amr_charger_smoke_abort. Core scenario: AMR encounters a pedestrian or temporary obstacle in its marked path; it slows or stops and proceeds only after the path is clear. Reference subject: autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: AMR, AGV, warehouse aisle, rack area, pedestrian crossing, or temporary blocked path with visible navigation lane. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: AMR encounters a pedestrian or temporary obstacle in its marked path; it slows or stops and proceeds only after the path is clear. Event graph: initial_state=Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop before the event.; trigger=a commanded robot motion, contact, grasp, clearance, or recovery step involving autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop; progression=robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop: AMR encounters a pedestrian or temporary obstacle in its marked path; it slows or stops and proceeds only after the path is clear | visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop; required_response=the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; terminal_state=contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible; critical_decision=whether the robot action is feasible, collision-safe, and useful for deployment or recovery judgment. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: AMR, AGV, warehouse aisle, rack area, pedestrian crossing, or temporary blocked path with visible navigation lane.. Application success criteria: a robotics user can judge whether the operation is feasible; motion respects kinematic limits, contact, and collision constraints; task progress is local and does not mutate unrelated scene structure. Misleading failure modes to penalize: robot links bend, detach, or pass through objects; tool or workpiece identity changes during manipulation; requested operation is replaced by camera drift or static display.
samples.video_generation_prompt: Use the reference image as the exact first frame and create a 5-second photorealistic industrial video of autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop: autonomous mobile robot warehouse path obstacle stop. Camera: locked static camera. Show a localized, causal event where requested motion/manipulation executes; by the end, final contact/clearance/grasp/placement/collision is visible. Preserve identity, component counts, materials, lighting, background, and non-event regions; only the requested event and camera perspective may change. Avoid text/logos/watermarks, extra entities, global regeneration, flicker, warping, disappearance, penetration, floating motion, and identity swaps.

Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Collaborative robot workstation with human proximity or handover table. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: collaborative robot workstation; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. samples.evaluation_prompt: FORGE-Bench evaluation prompt. Domain x Task cell: domain=embodied_robotics; abstract_task=industrial_logic_and_compliance. Task objective: test industrial_logic_and_compliance capability inside the embodied_robotics industrial domain. Scene family: erob_cobot_safety_scanner_slowdown. Core scenario: A worker enters the safeguarded operating area; the machine remains stopped or enters a protective stop until the area is clear. Reference subject: industrial machine safeguarded work area protective stop. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Press line, automated machine row, robot cell, or safeguarded industrial workstation with reachable operating area. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: industrial machine safeguarded work area protective stop; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (industrial machine safeguarded work area protective stop); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Press line, automated machine row, robot cell, or safeguarded industrial workstation with reachable operating area.. Task objective: test topology_mutation_and_failure capability inside the embodied_robotics industrial domain. Scene family: erob_gripper_failure_recovery. Core scenario: Gripper partially slips or one suction cup fails; local failure appears while the robot structure remains rigid. Reference subject: robot gripper suction cup. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a controlled dolly-in toward the local defect or failure region; target motion value 1.5. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Gripper, suction cup, end effector, or robot tool with visible grasped object. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: Gripper partially slips or one suction cup fails; local failure appears while the robot structure remains rigid. Event graph: initial_state=Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing robot gripper suction cup before the event.; trigger=a commanded robot motion, contact, grasp, clearance, or recovery step involving robot gripper suction cup; progression=robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: robot gripper suction cup: Gripper partially slips or one suction cup fails; local failure appears while the robot structure remains rigid | visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for robot gripper suction cup; required_response=the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; terminal_state=contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible; critical_decision=whether the robot action is feasible, collision-safe, and useful for deployment or recovery judgment. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: robot gripper suction cup; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (robot gripper suction cup); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Gripper, suction cup, end effector, or robot tool with visible grasped object. Application success criteria: a robotics user can judge whether the operation is feasible; motion respects kinematic limits, contact, and collision constraints; task progress is local and does not mutate unrelated scene structure. Misleading failure modes to penalize: robot links bend, detach, or pass through objects; tool or workpiece identity changes during manipulation; requested operation is replaced by camera drift or static display.

Preserve identity, component counts, materials, lighting, background, and non-event regions; only the requested event and camera perspective may change. Avoid text/logos/watermarks, extra entities, global regeneration, flicker, warping, disappearance, penetration, floating motion, and identity swaps.

Core scenario: Gripper partially slips or one suction cup fails; local failure appears while the robot structure remains rigid. Reference subject: robot gripper suction cup. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a controlled dolly-in toward the local defect or failure region; target motion value 1.5. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Gripper, suction cup, end effector, or robot tool with visible grasped object. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: robot gripper suction cup; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (robot gripper suction cup); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Gripper, suction cup, end effector, or robot tool with visible grasped object. Core scenario: Quadruped head camera traverses complex rubble/stairs without body identity changes or impossible foot contacts. Reference subject: quadruped robot industrial stairs. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a smooth left-to-right inspection pan; target motion value horizontal_pan_lr. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Quadruped robot or legged robot in industrial stairs, tunnel, plant, or debris setting. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.35, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.00, physical_plausibility=1.00, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.75, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=robotic_operation. Application objective: Evaluate whether generated robot or machine operation videos preserve actionable geometry, contact, and task progress. Scenario: Quadruped head camera traverses complex rubble/stairs without body identity changes or impossible foot contacts. Event graph: initial_state=Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing quadruped robot industrial stairs before the event.; trigger=a commanded robot motion, contact, grasp, clearance, or recovery step involving quadruped robot industrial stairs; progression=robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: quadruped robot industrial stairs: Quadruped head camera traverses complex rubble/stairs without body identity changes or impossible foot contacts | visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for quadruped robot industrial stairs; required_response=the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; terminal_state=contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible; critical_decision=whether the robot action is feasible, collision-safe, and useful for deployment or recovery judgment. Required observable events: robot, tool, workpiece, and target area remain visually identifiable: quadruped robot industrial stairs; the requested motion or manipulation step is executed; contact, clearance, grasp, placement, or collision state is visible. Decision-relevant elements: joint configuration and end-effector pose (quadruped robot industrial stairs); tool-to-object contact relationship; workspace obstacles, fixtures, and target alignment; reference-image requirement: Quadruped robot or legged robot in industrial stairs, tunnel, plant, or debris setting. Application success criteria: a robotics user can judge whether the operation is feasible; motion respects kinematic limits, contact, and collision constraints; task progress is local and does not mutate unrelated scene structure. Misleading failure modes to penalize: robot links bend, detach, or pass through objects; tool or workpiece identity changes during manipulation; requested operation is replaced by camera drift or static display.
samples.video_generation_prompt: Use the reference image as the exact first frame and create a 5-second photorealistic industrial video of quadruped robot industrial stairs: Quadruped head camera traverses complex rubble/stairs without body identity changes or impossible foot contacts. Camera: smooth left-to-right inspection pan, not orbit. Show a localized, causal event where requested motion/manipulation executes; by the end, final contact/clearance/grasp/placement/collision is visible. Preserve identity, component counts, materials, lighting, background, and non-event regions; only the requested event and camera perspective may change. Avoid text/logos/watermarks, extra entities, global regeneration, flicker, warping, disappearance, penetration, floating motion, and identity swaps.

samples.application_value: Rigid mechanisms, robotic arms, cranes, CNC machines, excavators, and multi-link equipment where coupled motion must stay feasible.

axis_rubric.geometric_integrity: Highest priority: links, rigid joints, axes, supports, and spatial topology must not drift, merge, or collapse.
axis_rubric.physical_plausibility: Motion must respect rigid-body coupling, load direction, contact, reachable poses, and classical mechanics.
axis_rubric.temporal_consistency: The same mechanism and parts must persist without flicker, detachment, identity swap, or soft-body melting.

sensitivity_variants.prompt_delta: Use slower motion and a wider view with fewer interacting elements.

Image requirement: Robot sanding, welding, drilling, or polishing tool in contact with surface. Core scenario: Local formwork support fails under load; collapse remains localized and follows support topology. Reference subject: construction formwork shoring scaffold. Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: perform a controlled dolly-in toward the local defect or failure region; target motion value 1.5. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Physical plausibility: obey gravity, contact, rigid-body coupling, load paths, pressure direction, fluid diffusion, heat/flame propagation, and feasible emergency dynamics. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Formwork, scaffold, temporary support, shoring tower, or concrete pouring support. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=heavy_operation_risk. Application objective: Assess whether heavy equipment, loads, supports, and worksite risks evolve plausibly for planning and supervision. Scenario: Local formwork support fails under load; collapse remains localized and follows support topology. Event graph: initial_state=Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing construction formwork shoring scaffold before the event.; trigger=a load, support, clearance, ground, or structural-risk change involving construction formwork shoring scaffold; progression=load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: construction formwork shoring scaffold: Local formwork support fails under load; collapse remains localized and follows support topology | visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for construction formwork shoring scaffold; required_response=the requested operation or failure progression occurs; terminal_state=final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation; critical_decision=whether the worksite risk, load path, support state, and personnel distance can be judged. Required observable events: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: construction formwork shoring scaffold; the requested operation or failure progression occurs; final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation. Decision-relevant elements: load path, rigging, outrigger, support, ground, or bridge alignment (construction formwork shoring scaffold); clearance to workers, vehicles, obstacles, or exclusion zones; motion direction, contact points, and structural deformation cues; reference-image requirement: Formwork, scaffold, temporary support, shoring tower, or concrete pouring support. Application success criteria: a site engineer can infer whether the operation remains safe; gravity, support, load transfer, and contact are physically credible; critical geometry and worksite context stay stable across frames. Misleading failure modes to penalize: suspended loads float or supports carry no visible load; equipment geometry changes instead of showing the requested risk; background or worksite layout regenerates during the event.

samples.application_objective: Assess whether heavy equipment, loads, supports, and worksite risks evolve plausibly for planning and supervision. Scenario: Lifted load approaches a structure; signaler triggers stop and load stabilizes before collision.
required_observable_events: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: hoist suspended load construction
the requested operation or failure progression occurs
final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation
decision_relevant_elements: load path, rigging, outrigger, support, ground, or bridge alignment (hoist suspended load construction)
clearance to workers, vehicles, obstacles, or exclusion zones
motion direction, contact points, and structural deformation cues
reference-image requirement: Hoist, hook, lifted load, scaffold, formwork, or nearby structure with exclusion zone
application_success_criteria: a site engineer can infer whether the operation remains safe
gravity, support, load transfer, and contact are physically credible
critical geometry and worksite context stay stable across frames
misleading_failure_modes: suspended loads float or supports carry no visible load
equipment geometry changes instead of showing the requested risk
background or worksite layout regenerates during the event

event_graph.initial_state: Reference-anchored stable industrial scene showing hoist suspended load construction before the event.
event_graph.trigger: a load, support, clearance, ground, or structural-risk change involving hoist suspended load construction
progression: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: hoist suspended load construction: Lifted load approaches a structure; signaler triggers stop and load stabilizes before collision
visible event progression remains localized and causally ordered for hoist suspended load construction
event_graph.required_response: the requested operation or failure progression occurs
event_graph.terminal_state: final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation
event_graph.critical_decision: whether the worksite risk, load path, support state, and personnel distance can be judged

Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Hoist, hook, lifted load, scaffold, formwork, or nearby structure with exclusion zone. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. required_observable_events: load, machine, support, worker, or worksite risk source is visible: construction trench broken pipe
the requested operation or failure progression occurs
final risk state is clear enough to judge stability or escalation

clearance to workers, vehicles, obstacles, or exclusion zones
motion direction, contact points, and structural deformation cues
reference-image requirement: Construction trench, tunnel, underground pipe, muddy water source, or excavation pit
application_success_criteria: a site engineer can infer whether the operation remains safe
gravity, support, load transfer, and contact are physically credible
critical geometry and worksite context stay stable across frames
misleading_failure_modes: suspended loads float or supports carry no visible load
equipment geometry changes instead of showing the requested risk
background or worksite layout regenerates during the event

Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Crane wire rope, sling, hoist cable, or hook block with visible tension path. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.80, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.10, physical_plausibility=1.05, reference_and_motion_fidelity=1.35, temporal_consistency=1.25. Application value layer: application_type=heavy_operation_risk. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Rail-guided maintenance bay, inspection pit, workshop track, or fixed industrial lane with a clear access boundary. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial rail inspection pit access isolation; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. machine state before and after the trigger

Motion requirement / viewpoint motion fidelity: hold a fixed monitoring view; no camera movement; target motion value 0.0. Evaluation dimensions: industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment, geometric_integrity, physical_plausibility, temporal_consistency, reference_and_motion_fidelity. Industrial logic and fact alignment: use state-machine style reasoning to verify causal closure, conditional triggers such as alarms or braking, compliance state, equipment roles, personnel/vehicle states, and industrial fact progression. Geometric integrity: preserve topology, rigid joints, load-bearing members, joint centers, dense periodic counts and spacing, local defect boundaries, component counts, and spatial relationships; only the requested failure or defect region may change. Temporal consistency: maintain object identity, material state, background, local event state, and cause-effect continuity without flicker, melting, role switching, or untriggered deformation. Reference and motion fidelity: execute the requested camera or viewpoint control while locking the reference identity, perspective, non-mutated regions, and background; apply static-video gating and region-isolated fidelity where relevant. Single-sample scoring gates: trigger floor vetoes for broken core logic, impossible physics, geometry collapse, static substitution on a motion task, or global regeneration outside the permitted local event region. Image requirement: Gate, loading dock, factory road, or restricted lane with clear vehicle path and access boundary. Execution constraints: do not add text overlays, subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra machines, or unrelated people; do not change component counts; do not replace the industrial scene with a different object. Dynamic scoring weights: geometric_integrity=1.05, industrial_logic_and_fact_alignment=1.85, physical_plausibility=1.25, reference_and_motion_fidelity=0.95, temporal_consistency=1.35. Required observable events: the unsafe trigger or violation is visually present: industrial gate vehicle restricted zone; the relevant alarm, stop, warning, or protective response is visible; the final state shows whether the hazard is contained or still active. Decision-relevant elements: worker or vehicle position relative to the danger zone (industrial gate vehicle restricted zone); PPE, barrier, signage, interlock, or alarm state; machine state before and after the trigger; reference-image requirement: Gate, loading dock, factory road, or restricted lane with clear vehicle path and access boundary.
